:::{#exr-mse-rss}
#### Mean squared error and residual sum of squares

For a regression model with conditional mean $\mean(x; \vth)$,
let $\fitted_i \eqdef \mean(x_i; \vth)$
be its predictions of $n \ge 1$ outcomes $y_1, \ldots, y_n$,
and let $\text{RSS}(\vth)$ (@def-rss) be taken over those same outcomes.
Write the [mean squared error](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-mse)
of these predictions in terms of $\text{RSS}(\vth)$,
and $\text{RSS}(\vth)$ in terms of that mean squared error.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-mse-rss}

First, each squared [prediction error](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-error)
equals the squared residual at $\vth$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\prederr_i^2
&= (\fitted_i - y_i)^2
&& \text{(definition of prediction error)}\\
&= \paren{\mean(x_i; \vth) - y_i}^2
&& \text{(definition of $\fitted_i$)}\\
&= \paren{-\paren{y_i - \mean(x_i; \vth)}}^2
&& \text{(factor out $-1$)}\\
&= \paren{-\resid_i(\vth)}^2
&& \text{(definition of $\resid_i(\vth)$)}\\
&= \resid_i(\vth)^2
&& \text{($(-a)^2 = a^2$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

So the mean squared error is the residual sum of squares divided by $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mselr{\fitted}
&= \frac{1}{n} \sumin \prederr_i^2
&& \text{(definition of mean squared error)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n} \sumin \resid_i(\vth)^2
&& \text{($\prederr_i^2 = \resid_i(\vth)^2$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n} \text{RSS}(\vth)
&& \text{(definition of RSS)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $\text{RSS}(\vth)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mselr{\fitted}
&= \frac{1}{n} \text{RSS}(\vth)
&& \text{(result above)}\\
n \, \mselr{\fitted}
&= \text{RSS}(\vth)
&& \text{(multiply both sides by $n$)}\\
\text{RSS}(\vth)
&= n \, \mselr{\fitted}
&& \text{(swap the two sides)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
